_readme: Example config for the electrical-contact / cutting-mask placement stage.
Runs AFTER grid_preperation -- point grid_preperation_output_dir at a real
grid_preperation --output folder (needs its flakes/ and cif/ subfolders,
plus the working template copy it produced).
All geometry numbers below are transcribed from contact_placement/materials/prompt.docx
-- see contact_placement/config.py's own field docstrings for the exact spec sentence
each one corresponds to. Units are real microns (um), same as everywhere else in this pipeline.
_comment_flake_filter: min_flake_score is flake_detection's OWN final_score (not re-derived -- grid_preperation just transforms flake_detection's real contour+score through its own calibration, see CifExportConfig.flake_detection_output_dir). No separate marker filter needed -- flake_detection already excludes marker/grid-dot regions before scoring.
_comment_chip_border_margin_um: No contact/cutting-mask geometry may be placed within this many um of the chip/die's real edge (derived from the working template's own B/P content, see cif_export.chip_bounds_from_cif) -- shrinks that boundary inward on all four sides before Hall/Ring placement.
_comment_user_tunable: These are the 'popping UI' parameters from the spec -- set here for headless/CLI runs, adjustable in the UI before committing to export.
_comment_num_to_try: With search.strategy "search": the most Hall / Ring placements allowed in the final layout (0 turns that mode off). With "greedy": the number of placement ATTEMPTS per mode (failed attempts count too).

search._comment: How flakes are chosen for contacts. 'objective' sets WHAT is maximised; flake_order / option_order / tie_break_by_score only steer the search (try-order), they never change the objective.
search._comment_strategy: options: "search" (DFS branch-and-bound over every flake's Hall/Ring options) | "greedy" (original one-pass placement in score order: all Hall attempts, then Ring)
search._comment_objective: options: "count" (number of placed flakes) | "score" (sum of placed flakes' scores) | "weighted" (count_weight + score_weight * flake_score - distance penalty, per placed flake)
search._comment_flake_order: options: "score" (highest score first) | "loaded" (file order: image name, then flake number). Heuristic only.
search._comment_option_order: options: "distance" (farthest pad distance first; Hall counts as farthest) | "score" (same for all options of one flake, so falls back to distance) | "weighted" (weighted value, best first). Heuristic only.
search._comment_tie_break_by_score: options: true | false. Among layouts with the same objective value, prefer the one with the higher total flake score.
search._comment_hall_weight: A Hall's objective value is multiplied by this (count: a Hall counts as hall_weight flakes, a Ring as 1), so Hall is preferred over Ring. 1.0 = no preference. Above 1 the search may place fewer flakes in total to get more Halls (with 1.5, 2 Halls beat 3 Rings).
search._comment_count_weight: "weighted" objective only: value each placed flake adds on its own.
search._comment_score_weight: "weighted" objective only: multiplier on the flake's score.
search._comment_distance_penalty_max: "weighted" objective only: subtracted for a Ring at the CLOSEST pad distance level; 0 at the farthest, linear in between. Hall has no distance penalty.
search._comment_ring_distance_levels: Number of pad distances tried per Ring exit side, evenly spaced from farthest to closest (x2 sides = Ring options per flake). strategy "search" only.
search._comment_max_steps: Search budget: number of option evaluations (one Hall/Ring option of one flake, in one search state). When reached, the best layout found so far is used.

hall._comment_voltage_taper_factor: Voltage contacts are voltage_width wide inside the new-flake rectangle, then widen linearly (trapezoid) to voltage_width * this at their far end. 1.0 = constant width.
hall._comment_voltage_side_bend_angle_deg: The 4 outer voltage taps bend this many degrees off the perpendicular at the new-flake rectangle edge, away from the centre tap. 0 = straight.

ring._comment_voltage_taper_factor: Voltage contacts widen linearly (trapezoid) from their grown width to width * this at the connecting end, starting just past the blocking rectangle (after the current contact), on the side away from the mask. 1.0 = plain rectangle.
ring._comment_ring_measurements: Per the spec's updated 'Ring:' measurements section. inner_ring/outer_ring are explicit min/max/step search ranges (config.frange); distance_between_arms/arm_width/finger_width are fixed constants, not searched.
